newsitem.title: USA: Continental Grain to pay US penalty on Iraqi sales.
newsitem.headline: Continental Grain to pay US penalty on Iraqi sales.

text.p: Continental Grain Co said Monday it would pay $25 million in a civil penalty and a subsidiary would pay a $10 million criminal fine to settle a dispute over eligibility for U.S. farm-export programs in making sales to Iraq.
In a statement, Continental, of New York, said it still would be able to participate in Agriculture Department programs to promote the export of U.S. farm products.
The subsidiary, Arab Finagrain Agri-Business Ltd, based in London, pleaded guilty to a one-count criminal charge in a separate settlement.
Continental said neither it nor its employees were found in violaton of the law.
The Justice Department was expected to make its own announcement later in the day about the matter.

At issue was Arab Finagrain's use of export credit guarantees to facilitate sales of U.S. farm products to Iraq. Continental contended the subsidiary was an "intervening purchaser," or intermediary, in the sales. The Justice Department said it was an unqualified co-exporter and ineligible for the loan guarantees.
Continental is one of the major grain exporters of the world.
The firm said it agreed to the settlement to avoid protracted litigation.
It said all of its sales to Iraq were completed before the invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
The disputed sales involved soybean meal and protein concentrate.

Arab Finagrain was incorporated in London with offices in Geneva. It was a joint marketing venture created by three partners -- a Continental subsidiary, Finagrain; the Paris bank Banque Arabe et Internationale d'Investissment; and Granflo, a Jordanian transport company.
